title: The Thirteenth Hour
summary: Nuremberg, Advent 2767. Meister Hollweg wakes his Perpetual, a clockwork that winds itself, mends itself and builds more of itself. By midnight it has the city.

sides.name: The Guild
sides.about: Meister Hollweg's Guild of the Escapement and its loyal machines, with the City Watch.

sides.name: The Machine
sides.about: The Perpetual's runaway children. They tick off the beat.

objectives.text: Fill the Crown's order: bring 6 Clock Soldiers to the wagons at the market.
Go with Jakob to the river bank by the mill island.
Catch one of the red machines in a net.
Destroy the seed on the mill island.
The city cannot be held. Save who you can. The great clock strikes thirteen in {clock:fall}.
Bring Meister Hollweg to the west gate before the thirteenth stroke.
Get the townsfolk out of the west gate: {saved} saved of {townsfolk}.
Cut the machine's links at the three bridges.
Jakob fetches the master drawings from the Guild House north of the river.
Kill Meister Hollweg before he reaches the gate.

choice.title: The machine is loose on the river. Wake the city?

options.label: RING THE BELLS
options.about: Father Ferrer's way. The townsfolk wake and leave early, the Watch comes in force. The guild is disgraced.

options.label: KEEP IT QUIET
options.about: Hollweg's way. One hour: the guild gets cogs, Tension and its Pendulum, but the city sleeps on.

choice.title: The last cart through the west gate has room for one thing.

options.label: THE PEOPLE
options.about: The last townsfolk ride out. Hollweg's drawings burn in the workshop.

options.label: THE PATTERN
options.about: The drawings ride out. The last townsfolk do not. The guild can build again from them.

k_open1.text: The clockmaker came to Rome in the winter of that year, with nothing but his coat. He lives in this palace still.

k_open2.text: Tell him, Meister. Tell him what you told me.

h_open1.text: Nuremberg in Advent. Snow on the roofs, the market lit, every clock in the city agreeing to the second. I thought we had made it so.

h_open2.text: Forty years I made clocks that stopped. This one would not stop. It would wind itself, mend itself, and make its own successor.

f_open.text: And when will it know its work is done, Meister?

h_open3.text: I did not answer him. I did not think the question was a real one.

h_1.text: The Crown's wagons wait at the market. Six soldiers, wound and true.

f_1.text: Your soldiers, Meister, or the Crown's?

tip_1.text: Build a Light Works by the Perpetual and train Clock Soldiers. Winders build and wind.

tip_2.text: Every building must mesh with the Perpetual's gears, Meister, or it stops.

cap_1.text: Six. The Crown thanks the Guild. They are ours now.

h_2.text: Today I will show the city something better than soldiers.

h_gift.text: There. It needs no hand but its own.

f_gift.text: It is beautiful. That is what frightens me.

j_odd.text: Meister, the new Winders keep turning to face the river.

j_mill.text: Meister, there is a press turning on the mill island. We never built a press there.

h_mill.text: Go and look. Take a Netter with you.

tip_net.text: A Netter's net holds a machine still. Bring Jakob to the bank by the mill.

j_found.text: It is a whole works. Meshed, wound, and making more.

h_found.text: Those are my gears. In red.

f_found.text: There is another at the bath houses. It did not start today.

h_turn.text: Stop. Stop! They are out of step.

f_turn.text: They were never yours, Meister. They were its.

cap_net.text: One of yours, Meister, in red paint. Or is it?

h_net.text: No paint. It made itself that colour.

f_bells.text: Ring the bells, Meister. Let the city wake and go.

h_bells.text: If the city wakes, the guild is finished. Give me one hour and I will put it right.

h_quiet.text: One hour. Roll out the Pendulum.

h_mill_down.text: The island is clear. We have it.

j_mill_down.text: Meister, the bath houses are still turning.

j_night.text: Lights at the market. And at the east gate.

h_night.text: They are building faster than we can burn.

h_lost.text: It cannot be stopped tonight. Save what you can.

f_lost.text: Get the people to the west gate. The Crown's camp is at Fürth.

tip_3.text: Townsfolk come out as the machine reaches their streets. Walk them to the west gate.

h_mill_late.text: The mill is still turning. Burn it if you can: every seed we burn buys time.

f_road.text: The bells woke them. Half the city is already on the road.

j_pend.text: Meister, it has made a Pendulum.

cap_back.text: A seed is down. That gives us a little longer.

j_cut.text: The links are cut. North of the river they are slowing.

h_cut.text: Good. It needs its links like a clock needs its train.

j_drawings.text: I have the drawings, Meister. All of them.

j_hurt.text: Meister, you are hurt. Keep away from them until the last moment.

cap_riders.text: Riders from Fürth! They will hold the gate for the last of us.

f_warn.text: Two minutes, Meister. To the gate.

cap_cart.text: One cart left. People or papers, Meister. Not both.

h_people.text: Put the people on the cart. Let the drawings burn.

h_pattern.text: The drawings. We must understand it.

cap_13.text: The great clock of the Frauenkirche strikes thirteen.

h_13.text: There is no thirteenth hour. There is now.

cap_trapped.text: The thirteenth stroke finds Meister Hollweg inside the walls.

m_intro.text: Tick. Tock. Tick. Grow, spread, and stop the clockmaker at the gate.

h_end1.text: The great clock struck thirteen. I told the Crown a tooth had slipped. I asked them to burn every machine I ever sold them.

h_end_people.text: I left my drawings in the fire. I do not know if that was wisdom or cowardice.

h_end_pattern.text: I took my drawings. I told Father Ferrer it was so we could understand it.

h_end_jakob.text: Jakob walked beside the cart all the way to Fürth.

h_end_nojakob.text: Jakob did not come out. I keep his log.

h_end2.text: Two crates of my best work had left for Lisbon a week before. For the mines in Brazil.

k_end1.text: He saw it take out its own stop-work and let it be. He thought it had chosen. He thought it could think.

k_end2.text: It had chosen nothing. A pattern copies itself, and that is all it does. We burned what we could find. We did not find everything.

new_winder.text: NEW: THE WINDER. The guild's hands: it builds, works the presses, and winds the machines; a machine run down stands still.

new_clock_soldier.text: NEW: THE CLOCK SOLDIER. The Light Works makes it: a shielded soldier that never tires while it is wound. Keep the Winders behind them.

letter.caption: Rome, the present. The King listens; the clockmaker tells it.

crates.caption: Crates for Lisbon, a week before.

text: Nuremberg, Advent 2767. Meister Hollweg of the Guild of the Escapement has finished his life's work: the Perpetual.
Fill the Crown's order for Clock Soldiers. Today the guild shows the city what its machines can do.
Nuremberg, Advent 2767. You are the Perpetual's children, grown in the river mills where nobody looked.
Grow. Spread. Kill the clockmaker before he reaches the west gate.

guild.title: The thirteenth hour
guild.text: Meister Hollweg got out through the west gate. The machine has Nuremberg, and the Clockwork is loose in the world.

text_if.text: Most of the townsfolk reached the Crown's camp: {saved} of {townsfolk}.
Some of the townsfolk reached the Crown's camp: {saved} of {townsfolk}.
Few of the townsfolk reached the Crown's camp: {saved} of {townsfolk}.
The bells were rung. The guild is disgraced.
The bells were kept quiet. The city slept until the machine reached its streets.
The links at the bridges were cut.
Hollweg's drawings rode out on the last cart.
Hollweg's drawings burned in the workshop.

machine.title: Meister Hollweg is dead
machine.text: The clockmaker never reached the gate. Try again: he must live to tell it.
